div.div: The manifest lists every rung. The player may switch between them at any segment boundary, because each segment starts with a keyframe.

div.div: Segments are 2–6 seconds. Shorter means faster reaction to a bandwidth change and more requests; longer means better compression and slower recovery. 4s is the usual compromise.

div.div: Bandwidth estimates lag and lie — a CDN burst reads as a fast link right before a stall. Buffer level is ground truth: it already reflects everything that actually happened. Use bandwidth to choose, and the buffer to overrule.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 756px; height: 1px; padding-top: 517px; margin-left: 40px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-warn-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-warn-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Never hand-roll ABR — hls.js or Shaka. What the interviewer wants is that you know the loop exists, that you step down fast and up slowly, and that a stall is far worse for a viewer than a lower resolution they will probably not notice.

a.text: Text is not SVG - cannot display
